record.paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Give characterizations of Arnoux-Rauzy words with a given balance.

evidence.quote: Give characterizations of Arnoux-Rauzy words with a given balance.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $A$ be a finite alphabet with $|A|\ge 2$. An infinite word $w\in A^{\mathbb N}$ is called an Arnoux–Rauzy word if, for every length $n\ge 0$, $w$ has exactly one left special factor and exactly one right special factor of length $n$, and each of these special factors can be extended (on the appropriate side) by every letter of $A$. (Equivalently, the factor complexity satisfies $p_w(n)=(|A|-1)n+1$ and the bispecial structure is the Arnoux–Rauzy one.)

For an integer $C\ge 1$, an infinite word $w$ over $A$ is said to be $C$-balanced if, for every letter $a\in A$ and for every pair of factors $u,v$ of $w$ with $|u|=|v|$, one has
$$\bigl||u|_a-|v|_a\bigr|\le C,$$
where $|x|_a$ denotes the number of occurrences of the letter $a$ in $x$. The word $w$ is called finitely balanced if it is $C$-balanced for some $C$.

Problem. Provide a characterization of those Arnoux–Rauzy words $w$ over $A$ that are $C$-balanced, for each fixed integer $C\ge 1$. More precisely, for a given $C$, describe in an effective way (for instance via a condition on the directive sequence of $w$) the set of all Arnoux–Rauzy words on $A$ which are $C$-balanced.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results are known. Sufficient conditions for $C$-balancedness of Arnoux–Rauzy words have been obtained, and a characterization is available if one replaces $C$-balance with the stronger notion of strong $C$-balance. However, even the case of 2-balanced ternary Arnoux–Rauzy words is not fully solved: it is shown that the prefixes of directive sequences of such words do not form a rational language, ruling out a rational-language characterization. Thus the general problem of characterizing Arnoux–Rauzy words with a given balance remains only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Balance properties of Arnoux-Rauzy words
status_evidence.snippet: Sufficient conditions for C-balancedness; characterization via strong C-balance; AR words need not be C-balanced for any C.
status_evidence.claim: Partial characterizations exist, replacing C-balance by strong C-balance.

status_evidence.title: Which Arnoux-Rauzy Words Are 2-Balanced?
status_evidence.snippet: The set of prefixes of directive sequences of 2-balanced ternary Arnoux-Rauzy words is not rational, so a rational-language characterization is impossible.
status_evidence.claim: Even the 2-balanced ternary case lacks a clean (rational) characterization.

status_evidence.title: Balancedness of Arnoux-Rauzy and Brun Words
status_evidence.snippet: Almost all AR words over arbitrary alphabets are finitely balanced; bounded strong partial quotients imply balancedness.
status_evidence.claim: Sufficient conditions for finite balancedness are known.
